sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: The **Parallel Governments** (Prati Sarkar) emerged as a direct consequence of the 'Do or Die' call, representing a shift from symbolic protest to **de facto sovereignty**.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: These governments functioned through **Janata Sarkars** (People's Governments), which replaced colonial administrative machinery in specific pockets.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: Key functions included **Nyayadan Mandals** (People's Courts) for dispute resolution, **Shanti Senas** (Peace Brigades) for security, and collection of local taxes to fund the movement.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The longevity and effectiveness of these governments were directly proportional to the **local support base** and the **geographical isolation** from British military hubs.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Key Application 1**: Social reform initiatives, including the prohibition of liquor and promotion of Khadi.
• **Key Application 2**: Resource mobilization through voluntary contributions to sustain the underground movement.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Severe British repression (Operation Zero Hour), lack of centralized coordination, and limited military resources.
• **Solutions**: Decentralized leadership and strong grassroots mobilization ensured survival despite the absence of top-tier Congress leadership.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'BTS' (Ballia, Tamluk, Satara).
• **Decoded Meaning**: B = Ballia (First), T = Tamluk (Bengal/Vidyut Vahini), S = Satara (Longest/Nana Patil).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Parallel Governments' of 1942 with the 'Provisional Government of Free India' (Azad Hind). Remember: Parallel Governments were internal/domestic; Azad Hind was external/exile-based.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Subaltern Agency' to describe how local peasants and workers sustained these governments, highlighting the democratic nature of the resistance.

keyTakeaways: Parallel governments represented the peak of the Quit India Movement's organizational capacity.
They demonstrated the ability of the Indian masses to self-govern, undermining the British claim of being the sole providers of order.
Satara remains the gold standard for the durability and administrative complexity of these movements.
